trunk-uat selects the newest develop commit with a successful trunk.yml push run and dist artifact; test plus a live run
release-artifacts.md and release-guide.md state the 'tag only a releasable commit' rule and how to find one
No change to admission rules, dist contents or how the dist is built
The selection rule is written into rv2r-02's context before rv2r-02 is prepared
context: Member of batch release-v2-remediation; ready now and runs alongside rv2r-01. DECISION GATE: any change to the admission contract (which runs or workflows may supply a releasable dist) goes to the owner. The retrospective's b8 metric '0 unreleasable commits' is replaced by 'release tooling always names the newest releasable commit', because releasing superseded commits would release untested code.
description: Since 2026-10-28, 42 of 100 trunk runs were cancelled: they were replaced while waiting under trunk.yml's workflow-level concurrency group `trunk-develop`. Admission (release-artifacts.md:41-45; scripts/release_admitted_dist.py:130) accepts only a dist from a successful trunk.yml push run on develop. Making a superseded commit releasable would therefore release code whose tests never ran, which breaks the ADR rule that a release ships only a trunk-tested exact commit. Implement: document 'tag only a commit with a successful trunk.yml push run'; make release-prep/release-check and trunk-uat (rv2r-02) select the newest such commit, and fail clearly otherwise, naming the newest releasable commit. Changing the admission contract (for example a separate dist workflow, or accepting superseded runs) is out of scope unless the owner decides otherwise. Rollback: revert this member's commits.
